purpose: Lower required-answer repetition. In revision 29, 467 of the 546 repeated answer slots are three- or four-letter connector words (3 letters: 141 repeats from 62 approvals; 4 letters: 326 repeats from 520 approvals).
method: Removed every exact Georgian string recorded in content/dictionaries/*.json, content/*.json, content/levels/*.json and docs/VOCABULARY* (approvals, exclusions, bonus-only reservations, rejected, skipped and unselected proposals, historical packs). Discovery: the 33 bonus-dictionary words outside the approved list (none has 3–5 letters and is unreviewed); English Wiktionary categories Georgian nouns (12,929) and Georgian adjectives (4,242), leaving 817 unrecorded 3–5-letter lemmas; Leipzig Georgian web 2019 and news 2016 corpora (1M sentences each) ranked by frequency; the batch-08 Bumbeishvili and Crubadan lists; and about 1,800 topic-brainstormed everyday words. Each proposed sense was checked on ganmarteba.ge (page SHA-256 recorded) or, where absent there, a fixed English Wiktionary revision (wikitext SHA-256 recorded). Plurals, verbs, pronouns, names, barbarisms, action senses, serious illnesses, spelling variants and uncommon technical words were screened out (listed under editorScreenedNotProposed).
poolFinding: The unreviewed pool of familiar 3–4-letter Georgian nouns and adjectives is close to exhausted: of about 1,800 brainstormed everyday words only 82 three-to-five-letter spellings were unrecorded, and the corpus and Wiktionary scans add mostly verbal nouns, inflected forms, names and rare words. This batch therefore has 83 candidates instead of about 100, mostly five letters; only three have three letters. Padding with obscure words would break the familiarity-first rule.

familiarityTiers.A: Everyday word most adult speakers use or hear regularly (editor judgment).
familiarityTiers.B: Familiar but less frequent, regional, bookish, rural or specialised; owner judgment especially needed.

trialReplan.method: Isolated copy of the revision-29 candidate search and planner (artifacts/journey-v29/plan in the revision-29 worktree), run in a scratch directory with identical settings: search.py 12 0 15 40; plan.py five --rounds 4 --rarity-scale 20000 --six-bonus 2000 --concentration 30. Same rules: 5/6/7 tiles, at most five rows, five answers, 75-level gap, pacing and variety. The control run with the 2,318 approvals reproduces revision 29.
trialReplan.note: Heuristic planner estimate, not a validated campaign. The 75-level gap was re-checked on the selected boards; production layout/runtime gates, the solve check and board review were not run.

inPlaceEstimate.method: Direct same-length substitution into the existing 500 revision-29 boards (wheel letters and crossing letters kept, at most one replaced repeated answer per board, maximum matching).
inPlaceEstimate.note: A conservative floor: fixed boards rarely accept a new word, so a re-plan is needed to realise most of the gain.

rankingMethod: Rank = number of usable 5-, 6- and 7-tile wheels (exact unions of two approved words that already hold five approved answers and the stage minimum of long answers) whose letters contain the candidate; ties by uses in the all-candidates trial re-plan, then length. More wheels means the word can act as a connector on more boards, which matters most for a 1,000-level campaign.
limitations: Owner review complete: all 83 rejected; nothing ingested or applied. Familiarity tiers are editorial judgments, not native-speaker review. Corpus counts come from news and web text and under-represent household, rural and food words. The trial re-plans are unvalidated drafts in a scratch directory; production dictionaries, policies, packs and saves are unchanged.
sourceAttribution: Georgian explanatory dictionary ganmarteba.ge (Linguistic Technologies Group); English Wiktionary contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0). Discovery only: Leipzig Corpora Collection Georgian web 2019 and news 2016 word lists (counts only, no text reproduced); Dato Bumbeishvili (MIT) and Kevin Scannell/Crubadan (CC BY 4.0) lists from targeted batch 08. Brief original English glosses; source definitions are not republished.
